title: Song of Solomon 5
paragraphs: ¹ "I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh and my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, dear friends! Drink — drink deeply of love!" ² I was asleep, but my heart was awake. I heard my beloved knocking: "Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my perfect one — my hair is wet with the dew, my locks with the drops of the night." ³ "I have already taken off my robe — must I put it on again? I have washed my feet — must I soil them?" ⁴ My beloved thrust his hand through the opening; my heart leaped within me. ⁵ I rose up to open for my beloved, and my hands dripped with myrrh — my fingers with flowing myrrh — on the handles of the bolt.

⁶ I opened for my beloved, but my beloved had gone — he had left. My heart sank when he spoke and turned away. I looked for him but could not find him; I called to him but he did not answer. ⁷ The watchmen making their rounds in the city found me — they struck me, they wounded me; the guards of the walls tore away my shawl. ⁸ I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem — if you find my beloved, tell him I am faint with love. ⁹ "How is your beloved better than any other, O most beautiful of women? How is your beloved better than any other, that you would have us search for him like this?" ¹⁰ "My beloved is radiant and ruddy, outstanding among ten thousand.

¹¹ His head is like the finest gold; his hair is wavy, black as a raven. ¹² His eyes are like doves beside the water streams, washed in milk, jewel-like in their setting. ¹³ His cheeks are like beds of spices yielding perfume; his lips are like lilies dripping with flowing myrrh. ¹⁴ His arms are like rounded gold, set with beryl; his body is like polished ivory adorned with lapis lazuli. ¹⁵ His legs are like pillars of marble set on bases of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, magnificent as its cedars.
¹⁶ His mouth is sweetness itself; he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem."
